title: LRU Cache
prompt: Design a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache. Implement the `LRUCache` class with a fixed `capacity`: `get(key)` returns the value if present (and marks it as recently used) or -1 if not; `put(key, value)` inserts or updates a value, evicting the least recently used entry if the cache is at capacity. Both operations should run in O(1) average time — directly relevant to KV-cache / model-artifact eviction in inference serving.
constraints: get and put must both run in O(1) average time

examples.input: cache = LRUCache(2); cache.put(1,1); cache.put(2,2); cache.get(1); cache.put(3,3); cache.get(2)

test_cases.expected: see prompt — sequence of operations, not a single call

hints: O(1) get/put suggests a hash map from key to node, plus a doubly linked list to track recency order.
On get, move the accessed node to the front (most recently used) end of the list.
On put at capacity, evict the node at the back (least recently used) end before inserting the new one.
Python's collections.OrderedDict gives you move_to_end and popitem(last=False) for free, if you'd rather not hand-roll the linked list.
